CHIEF COMPLAINT
Chest pain (resolved)

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a new patient with referral from the emergency room for evaluation of possible esophagitis. She reports experiencing chest pain in early October 2020 that lasted 4 days. The pain occurred randomly, without a clear trigger at onset. She describes the pain as sharp, located in the center of the chest behind the breastbone, and felt like she was having a heart attack. Nothing she did relieved the pain, so she went to the emergency room. At that time, she underwent EKG and blood tests, which were all normal. The patient also reports associated difficulty swallowing and possibly heartburn at the time, though she states she has never had heartburn before and was uncertain what heartburn feels like. She notes the pain was worse with eating. All symptoms, including chest pain and difficulty swallowing, resolved approximately 3 days after the ER visit. The patient has remained asymptomatic for 3 months since the initial episode but reports feeling like something is wrong. She notes she needed this appointment 3 months ago when symptoms first occurred but this was the first available appointment. She recalls experiencing a stressful job transition around the time of the chest pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies abdominal pain and reports normal bowel movements. She denies prior experience with heartburn.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids, anemia, cholecystectomy (several years ago)

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Patient denies awareness of family history of gastrointestinal problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is attempting to lose weight. She experienced a stressful job transition around the time of symptom onset.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen: Mild tenderness to light palpation in upper abdominal quadrants bilaterally. Lower abdomen non-tender to palpation. Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
EKG from ER: normal. Blood tests from ER: normal. Cardiac workup from ER: normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient with history of acute onset chest pain with associated dysphagia and possible heartburn from 3 months ago, now completely resolved and asymptomatic for 3 months. Differential diagnosis includes anxiety, esophagitis, gastroesophageal reflux disease, dyspepsia, and musculoskeletal etiologies. Cardiac etiology ruled out by ER testing including normal EKG, blood tests, and cardiac workup. Clinical presentation with stressful job transition at time of symptom onset suggests anxiety as likely contributing factor, with possible musculoskeletal contribution. Given 3-month asymptomatic period, any esophagitis would likely have healed by now. Discussed options of upper endoscopy (EGD) versus symptomatic monitoring. Patient elected to self-monitor symptoms and will contact the office if she experiences recurrence of chest pain or other concerning symptoms. If symptoms recur, will schedule EGD for further evaluation. Otherwise, patient to follow up as needed for any gastrointestinal complaints.
